claims.text: The multi-phase eutectic high-entropy alloy possesses a naturally formed protective oxide layer.
The alloy has distinct eutectic phases with different electrochemical potentials.
Elevated temperature destabilizes the protective oxide film.
Mechanical wear removes the protective oxide film.
Removal of the oxide film exposes the electrochemically distinct phases.
Electrochemical disparities among exposed phases initiate localized micro-galvanic corrosion.
Micro-galvanic interactions accelerate the corrosion rate.
Corrosion products and localized corrosion roughen the worn surface.
Corrosion reduces the mechanical integrity and cohesion of the worn surface.
A rougher and less cohesive corroded surface exacerbates subsequent wear.
Reciprocal enhancement of wear and corrosion creates a positive feedback loop.
Simultaneous elevated-temperature wear and corrosion produce a significantly higher total degradation rate than the stated isolated or lower-temperature baselines.
The wear rate is higher under coupled conditions because the protective oxide layer is absent.
The proposed mechanism applies only when wear removes nascent protection faster than effective protection can persist or reform.
Less aggressive media or changes in phase distribution may alter film formation or wear mechanisms enough to invalidate the proposed behavior.

contradictions.description: The prediction compares coupled degradation with either isolated wear, isolated corrosion, or a lower-temperature condition, whereas the falsification rule requires coupled degradation to exceed the sum of isolated wear and corrosion. A result could therefore satisfy the stated prediction by exceeding either individual baseline but still be declared falsifying because it does not exceed their sum.
